newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges steady, one pct offers to rise.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges steady, one pct offers to rise.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges ended steady on Tuesday after traders' perceptions of higher numbers failed to materialise, while some sellers of low sulphur cargoes said they would raise prices in line with stronger demand.

High sulphur barges traded as high as $83.50 fob ARA for specific delivery, the same as a day earlier, and $83 for normal delivery, after earlier deals 50 cents to $1 lower. This compared with Monday's closing levels of $82.50/$83.
There was unconfirmed talk of $84 being done, but other traders dismissed this. Some market players said earlier they believed it would climb to that level with avails tighter and demand improving.
Rotterdam bunker prices were little changed with demand said to average up to 15,000 tonnes. 380 CST fuel was priced at $84/85 a tonne, with 180 CST at $90/91 and Antwerp prices were $1 higher.
Low sulphur barges traded a little higher. Most buyers were steady at $94 and sellers held their ground at the $96 mark, with a small deal done at $95.75 fob, or some 75 cents up on a deal last week.

The buyer, a Rotterdam-based French refiner, said he paid the higher number for a 1,700 tonne barge of one percent sulphur fuel "as we need to load on Friday and the seller said he did not have a lot of product."
He added: "I started bidding at $94, then $95, but nobody was interested...Sellers are at $96".
High sulphur cargoes continued to draw strength from Russian cargoes that are finding homes at steady prices.
Traders said a French refiner sold a cracked M-100 at two means plus $1.50/$2, a touch lower than its original asking price but about the same it paid for it recently.
Two other Russian cargoes were heard traded also but no further details were available.

One percent was also steady, with a stable supply demand picture and with crude and swaps stronger. At least two sellers, a U.K. refiner and a Spanish refiner, and two buyers were heard to be on the market.

Rumours were rife the U.K. refiner sold its cargo to an independent trader but the refiner said it was still holding the low sulphur material and will try to up its asking price of $94.50 fob by $1.5 to $2 on Wednesday.

"We will try to bring it to the $96 level...It seems demand is rising. There's one trader interested in the cargo, a refiner is a potential buyer and there's also some internal demand," the refiner said.
"We perceive the market is tightening a little," the refiner added. A seller who was not actively offering his material said he would ask more than $95 fob for it.
But other traders said these numbers were unattainable and there was no justification for a rise.
